value.rationale: Counting minimal-rank square-zero factors of a fixed singular matrix is a natural strengthening of structural factorability criteria: existence alone cannot distinguish the two trace strata or the rank profile of an idempotent factor. The theorem gives full higher-dimensional multiplicities and a strict rank-by-rank trace separation for every field size, structurally explained by constrained Grassmannian complements; the n=2 previously known specialization is not claimed as new.
